healthcareSystem: State-funded universal system for residents. Tourists pay out-of-pocket. Public hospitals are free for emergencies but quality varies. Private clinics offer better care.
qualityNotes: Public hospitals in Algiers provide basic care but are overcrowded. Private clinics in Algiers and Oran offer better quality. English-speaking doctors are rare — French is the medical language. Rural healthcare is very limited.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 8am-8pm Saturday-Thursday; rotating night pharmacies (pharmacie de garde) in each neighborhood
pharmacyTips: Look for 'Pharmacie' signs with a green cross. Pharmacies are common in cities. Pharmacists are well-trained (French system) and can recommend OTC medications. Communication is in French and Arabic — English is rare.
prescriptionRules: Algeria follows French-style pharmacy regulations. Most common medications are available OTC. Antibiotics officially require a prescription but enforcement varies. Controlled substances strictly require a prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled narcotics (opioids, tramadol)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (benzodiazepines, stimulants)
restrictedMeds.note: ADHD stimulant medications may not be available or recognized. Bring documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis-based products
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in all forms in Algeria with severe penalties.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in French and English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, bring the original prescription. French-language documentation is strongly preferred.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is recommended. Private clinics in Algiers are affordable but may not meet Western standards for complex procedures. Evacuation to France or Tunisia may be necessary for serious conditions.

recommended: Rabies (for extended rural or desert travel)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for entry from most countries. Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date.

waterNotes: Tap water in Algiers and major cities is generally treated but bottled water is recommended for visitors. In southern desert regions and rural areas, always use bottled water.
foodSafetyTips: Food in established restaurants is generally safe. Algerian cuisine is well-cooked (couscous, tajine, chorba). Be cautious with salads and raw vegetables at street stalls. Avoid tap water ice. Peel fruits before eating.
medicalTourismNote: Algeria is not a medical tourism destination. Travelers needing advanced medical care are typically referred to France or Tunisia.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Algeria. Emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, hospital info, vaccination advice, and travel insurance guidance.

dentalCare.availability: Dental care available in Algiers and major cities. Private clinics offer decent care.
dentalCare.costRange: $10-30 for a consultation; $15-50 for fillings; $10-40 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Algiers follow French dental standards. Dentists are well-trained but facilities may be basic. Communication in French.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, visit a private dental clinic (cabinet dentaire). Night and weekend duty pharmacies can provide pain relief — check the local 'pharmacie de garde' schedule posted at pharmacy doors.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: No dedicated English-language crisis line — contact your embassy
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Extremely limited. French-speaking therapists available in Algiers.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services in English are essentially unavailable. French-speaking psychologists and psychiatrists can be found in Algiers. Mental health stigma is significant.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited. Cities have uneven sidewalks, few ramps, and limited elevator access.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Newer private clinics have basic wheelchair access. Public hospitals often lack proper accessibility features.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public transport is not wheelchair accessible. Taxis are the primary option. The Algiers Metro has some accessible stations.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Algeria's historic Casbah and medina areas are extremely challenging for wheelchair users. Plan carefully and consider hiring local assistance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. Masks may be requested in some healthcare facilities.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at private labs in Algiers. Limited availability outside major cities.
covidStatus.notes: All COVID entry restrictions have been lifted.

insuranceClaimProcess: Pay upfront at all facilities (cash preferred — Algerian dinar or euros). Keep all receipts and medical documentation. Request French-language documents (English may not be available). File claims with your insurer upon return.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Healthcare is very affordable. Public emergency care (SAMU) is free. Private clinics charge moderate fees.

medicalEvacuation.note: France is the traditional evacuation destination due to language and medical ties. Tunisia is closer and has good hospitals. Air evacuation from southern desert regions is logistically complex.
